label: Product Merchan­dising Card
title: Product Merchan­dising Card
summary: Use a Product Merchandising Card to promote one product or campaign on a photo, with a badge, a short title, and one action.
corePrinciple: The photo sells; the footer names it and acts.

anatomy.title: A photo, a corner, and a footer
anatomy.description: The photo fills a 223 px card with 12 px corners. A header row sits on its top edge, the avatar at the left and a badge at the right, and the footer sits on its bottom edge: a glass badge, the title and subtitle, and the Button.

configuration.title: Badges, an avatar, and one look for both
configuration.description: imageSource is the photo; the card has none of its own. badgeLabel adds a lilac badge at the top right and specialBadgeLabel a frosted glass Badge above the title; each stays hidden without a label, and badgeIcon and specialBadgeIcon put an Icon before it. avatarSource shows a round picture at the top left, avatarMonogram initials instead, and showAvatar={false} removes it. ctaLabel and onCtaPress make the small purple Button. One modes object styles the corner badge and the Button together: AppearanceBrand Primary turns both gold, and Emphasis, Badge Size, and Button / Size change them too. badge, avatar, specialBadge, and cta replace those parts and don’t get the card’s modes.

states.title: The Button acts, or the whole card does
states.description: The card isn’t pressable: its Button is. onPress makes the whole card one button that dims slightly while pressed, announced by accessibilityLabel or the title. Open stays a separate button inside it, so use one or the other: cta={false} drops the Button. There’s no selected, disabled, or loading look.
blocks: cta={false}: the card is the one target.

sizing.title: 223 px tall, as wide as its host
sizing.description: The card is 223 px tall unless you set height, and takes its width from its host; Figma draws it at 328 px. The photo fills and crops to the card. The header and footer sit on the photo: the footer grows upward with its content, and in a narrow card the Button drops under the title. The title and subtitle stay on one line and end in … unless disableTruncation is set.
blocks: At 168 px the Button drops under the title.
Each ends in … on one line.
They wrap, and the footer grows upward.

content.title: A short name, one line, a verb
content.description: Make the title the product or campaign in two to four words, and the subtitle one line of support. Badge labels are a word or two, such as New or Zero balance, and ctaLabel a verb, such as Open or Buy. Pass accessibilityLabel with the offer: the photo tells a screen reader nothing.

sources.title: Use the public Product Merchandising Card contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (19 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Product Merchandising card has the booleans avatar, gradient, showBadge, and showSpecialBadge and the text title and subtitle; the package shows each badge only when you pass its label and has no gradient. Figma darkens the footer with a black gradient, while the package draws only a blurred copy of the photo, so the white text sits on a pale haze, with a lighter band where the copy is re-cropped. Badge icons and the badge, avatar, specialBadge, and cta slots don’t get the card’s modes. Without avatarSource or avatarMonogram the avatar is a stock portrait, and without imageSource the card has no background. The header and footer are a few pixels taller than Figma’s. The published Storybook still shows the older generated page (all reported).
